title: Analytical advances in citrus disease detection: Conventional molecular assays and emerging analytical technologies

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Analytical advances in citrus disease detection: Conventional molecular assays and emerging analytical technologies》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Abstract · abstract-1-1】Citrus diseases caused by fungal, bacterial, and viral pathogens continue to threaten global citrus production, creating an urgent need for analytical technologies that enable accurate, rapid, and field-deployable disease diagnosis.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Analytical advances in citrus disease detection: Conventional molecular assays and emerging analytical technologies》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Abstract · abstract-1-3】Particular emphasis is placed on analytical performance, including sensitivity, selectivity, reproducibility, matrix effects, analytical robustness, and practical applicability, as well as on the contribution of nanomaterials and advanced sensing interfaces to improving analytical capability.

【Abstract · abstract-1-8】Overall, the evidence indicates that future citrus disease diagnostics will rely on interoperable and complementary analytical workflows that integrate molecular specificity with electrochemical, spectroscopic, imaging, and computational technologies to enable early disease detection, precision phytosanitary management, and robust decision-making under real agricultural conditions.

evidence.text: Particular emphasis is placed on analytical performance, including sensitivity, selectivity, reproducibility, matrix effects, analytical robustness, and practical applicability, as well as on the contribution of nanomaterials and advanced sensing interfaces to improving analytical capability.

Overall, the evidence indicates that future citrus disease diagnostics will rely on interoperable and complementary analytical workflows that integrate molecular specificity with electrochemical, spectroscopic, imaging, and computational technologies to enable early disease detection, precision phytosanitary management, and robust decision-making under real agricultural conditions.
